_comment: MQTT link behavior as data. The tests run the link against real Mosquitto brokers, where a failed login is CONNACK 5 ('Connection refused: Not authorized'), never 4. 'credentials': mqtt_link.js pastes MQTT_USERNAME/MQTT_PASSWORD unescaped into mqtt://USER:PASS@HOST:PORT. expected_broker_username/expected_broker_password are what the broker receives in CONNECT (null: the packet has no password field); the outcome against a broker that has an account with exactly those credentials is that the link connects, unless expected_login is 'refused' (a broker that checks passwords, as Mosquitto does, cannot authenticate a username that arrives without one). expected_connect_error: the failure never reaches the configured broker; after_ms is how long it takes (fake clock) and expected_dialed is the host and port the bridge dials instead of the broker when the URL breaks (the username survives as the host name). Identical on Node 10.14 and Node 24. 'connack_refusals': a CONNACK with a non-zero return code makes the connection attempt fail with this error (forged in the tests: Mosquitto 2.1 answers a failed login with 5). 'commands': MQTT messages received by the bridge and the panel requests they cause; expected_panel_requests is an unordered list of request lines. The bridge subscribes to paradox/command/arm and paradox/command/disarm only, so a real broker never delivers a row with delivered_by_broker false: such rows pin the bridge's own topic matching and are delivered by hand. 'broker_ports': what the bridge dials for a given MQTT_PORT string (the host is always MQTT_HOSTNAME); unparsable values silently become the MQTT default 1883. 'broker_hosts': what the bridge dials for a given MQTT_HOSTNAME/MQTT_PORT pair, because the host is pasted unescaped into the same URL. Rows that pin a defect on purpose (known_bug) are in known_bugs/mqtt.json, in the same groups.

credentials.name: '@' in the password
credentials.note: the URL parser splits at the last '@', so this survives

credentials.name: leading and trailing spaces in the password
unicode letters and a currency sign
':' in the username only
credentials.note: correct only by luck: the client splits user:pass at the LAST ':'

credentials.name: trailing ':' in the password
credentials.note: correct by the same luck: the last ':' that is followed by something is the separator

broker_ports.name: port above 65535
broker_ports.note: rejected immediately, nothing logged, no connection attempt

broker_hosts.name: upper case is folded to lower case
IPv6 address in brackets
broker_hosts.note: works only because the user typed the brackets

broker_hosts.name: non-ASCII host name is converted to punycode

connack_refusals.name: return code 4 (bad username or password)
connack_refusals.expected_error_message: Connection refused: Bad username or password
connack_refusals.note: Mosquitto 2.1 answers a failed login with 5 instead, so the tests forge this code

connack_refusals.name: return code 5 (not authorized)
connack_refusals.note: what Mosquitto answers to a failed login, whether the user is unknown or only the password is wrong

connack_refusals.name: reserved return code 6
connack_refusals.note: the message text comes from the mqtt library, which has no entry for this code; only 'any non-zero code fails the connect' matters

commands.name: two arm messages arm twice (no de-duplication)
arm and disarm messages each send their own request
topic must match exactly: extra level
topic must match exactly: trailing slash
topic must match exactly: other prefix
the bridge's own status topic is ignored
